text:
Charlie McAvoy has 9 points and one goal in 16 games, which undersells how the Bruins play with him. Boston takes 63.5% of the expected goals at five on five (the quality of chances) when he's on the ice, 12.9 points better than without him, and he does it in 24 minutes a night against top opposition.

The scoring is the soft spot. He's pointless in four straight on 2.5 expected points, and our numbers say the chances are there. He's shooting 4% on 25 shots, and the Bruins have scored 2.7 fewer goals than expected with him on the ice. That's the kind of gap that closes.

The week had some noise. He fought Bobby Brink in a 6-2 loss to Minnesota and faced talk of a suspension, but he played both games since. Last season Evolving-Hockey had him 30th among 215 defensemen and his competition in the 95th percentile, and The Athletic just wrote about how much he and Minnesota's Brock Faber look and play alike. Watch the assists: the possession says they're coming.
headline: McAvoy's team wins his minutes; the points lag
